limitations: Card colors are assigned by a random shuffle, so no check can predict which two cards match or how many moves a full game takes.
Win message and matched-pair persistence cannot be reliably reached without knowing the shuffled deck order; matching behavior and win state are not asserted.
Cards are div elements with role=button; disabled-state assertions only apply to native form controls, so card interactivity is not checked via disabled.
Timed flip-back (800ms) and lockBoard behavior depend on timing, which is outside the allowed action model.
Visual appearance (colors, pixel styling, transitions, responsive layout) cannot be verified through DOM text/visibility assertions.
Assertions target the first two board children by position; their colors are random, so only counter behavior, not match outcome, is checked.

# Pixel Memory Match

A simple, offline browser-based memory match game with 8 pairs of colored cards.

## Features

- 8 pairs of colored cards (16 total)
- Flip two cards at a time
- Matched pairs stay open
- Move counter
- Win message when all pairs are matched
- New Game button to reset
- Keyboard accessible (Tab to focus, Enter/Space to flip)
- Responsive layout down to 360px wide

## How to Play

1. Open `index.html` in any modern browser.
2. Click or press Enter/Space on a card to flip it.
3. Flip a second card to try to find a match.
4. If the colors match, the cards stay open. If not, they flip back.
5. Keep going until all 8 pairs are matched.
6. The move counter tracks how many attempts you've made.
7. Click "New Game" to start over.

## Tech Stack

- HTML5
- CSS3 (custom properties, grid, transitions)
- Plain JavaScript (no libraries or frameworks)

## Offline

No network requests, external assets, or server code. Everything is contained in the three files.

## Files

- `index.html` — structure
- `style.css` — styling
- `script.js` — game logic
